page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance features 30.0 GB of system memory, translating to 7.62 GB per physical core, and includes a dedicated local storage allocation of 950 GB delivered via NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline speed of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the compute and memory subsystems operate in lower performance tiers compared to modern hardware. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth for large, uncached blocks is also limited, registering at 22.62 GB/sec for read operations and 14.23 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic and database operations, such as Redis SET performance at 2.54 million operations per second, place the instance in the bottom 25% tier.

From a resource-density perspective, the i3.xlarge offers a qualitative tradeoff by pairing a substantial 950 GB local NVMe SSD with 30.0 GB of RAM on an older CPU architecture. While raw processing power and memory throughput are weak relative to newer generations, the instance provides a cost-efficient profile for workloads that require high-capacity, low-latency local storage without demanding high-performance CPU compute.

This instance configuration is suited for storage-intensive workloads that do not require intensive CPU calculations. Appropriate applications include transactional databases, NoSQL databases, caching layers, and moderate web serving operations where local NVMe storage speed is the primary bottleneck rather than raw processing throughput.

The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of RAM and a dedicated 950 GB local NVMe SSD. Benchmark data indicates that compute and memory performance are modest, with CPU and memory bandwidth results falling into the lower percentiles. Consequently, this instance represents a qualitative tradeoff, offering substantial local storage capacity and moderate memory at the expense of raw processing power. It is best suited for storage-centric applications, such as NoSQL databases, caching layers, and transactional databases that benefit from direct NVMe storage access.
